message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: The player is putting Forest on the bottom of their library, but Forest is their only green source alongside Haven of the Spirit Dragon (which only adds colored mana for Dragon creature spells). Looking at their hand, they have Commander's Sphere (3 mana), Dragon's Hoard (3 mana), Bag of Tricks (needs green), Rishkar's Expertise (needs double green), and Skyship Stalker (needs double red). With Vrondiss as their commander (costs 3RG), they desperately need green mana. Forest is one of the most critical cards in this hand as a basic land that produces green. Rishkar's Expertise is a 6-mana spell that requires double green and creatures with power to be effective - it's the most cuttable card in this opening hand since it won't be castable for many turns and requires board presence.

message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: In the mulligan/bottom decision for a 6-card hand (after mulligan to 6), the player needs to put one card on the bottom. The hand has only one land (Mountain) plus Bojuka Bog (enters tapped), with Rakdos Signet and Mind Stone as 2-mana rocks. Keeping both 2-mana rocks is important for acceleration, but Unstable Obelisk at 3 mana is also a ramp piece and removal. However, the real concern is that Hex at 6 mana is very expensive and requires exactly 6 target creatures to be legal - it's often a dead card. Bottoming Hex instead of Unstable Obelisk would preserve more versatility, as Unstable Obelisk provides both ramp and permanent removal. That said, Unstable Obelisk is slow and the hand already has two cheaper rocks, so this is debatable.

On turn 1, playing Forest instead of Haven of the Spirit Dragon is slightly suboptimal. The hand contains Dragon's Hoard (3 colorless), Commander's Sphere (3 colorless), and Bag of Tricks (1G). Haven of the Spirit Dragon produces colorless mana and can also produce colored mana specifically for Dragon creature spells (like Skyship Stalker). Forest only produces green. Since the player needs colorless mana for their 3-drop artifacts on turn 2-3 anyway, and Haven can serve double duty by also casting Dragons later, Haven would have been slightly better as the turn 1 land drop, saving Forest for turn 2 when green mana might be needed for Bag of Tricks.

Shadowblood Ridge requires {1} to activate for colored mana, making it worse than Swamp as an early land drop. Playing Swamp now gives free {B} every turn, while Shadowblood Ridge could be played later when there's spare mana to activate it.

Returning Gruul Turf to itself means you replay it tapped next turn, losing a full turn of mana development. The Turf enters tapped again and triggers the bounce again, creating a loop where you never gain the extra mana. You effectively waste your land drop this turn and next turn. Returning Forest or Haven of the Spirit Dragon would let the Turf stay in play producing RG, and you'd replay the basic/utility land next turn untapped, netting +1 mana going forward.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Mind Stone
chosen_display: 2. {1}, {T}, Sacrifice Mind Stone: Draw a card.
annotation_description: On turn 3 with only 3 lands and expensive cards in hand (Solemn Simulacrum at 4, Combustible Gearhulk at 6, Blasphemous Act potentially expensive), sacrificing Mind Stone for a card draw is terrible. Mind Stone is needed as a mana source to cast Solemn Simulacrum on turn 4 (which would fetch another land) or to ramp toward the expensive spells in hand. Drawing a card when you're mana-starved and have a hand full of 4+ mana spells sets you back significantly. The player is giving up a mana rock they desperately need for tempo.

With only 2 lands in play, GPT5n should prioritize developing mana. Playing Talisman of Indulgence would provide mana acceleration needed to cast expensive cards like Etali (6 mana) and Marionette Master (6 mana). Warlock Class's level 1 ability only triggers if a creature died this turn at end step - and with very few creatures on the board across all players, it provides minimal value right now. The Talisman immediately adds a mana source, accelerating toward powerful plays. Alternatively, playing Mountain first (land drop) then Talisman would be even better sequencing, but playing Warlock Class over Talisman is the key mistake - it delays mana development for a card that does very little at level 1 in the current board state.

With only 2 lands on the battlefield (Shadowblood Ridge, Swamp) and expensive cards in hand (Etali at 6 mana, Marionette Master at 6 mana), discarding a Mountain loses a critical land drop. Rakdos Carnarium is the only other land in hand but it bounces a land, so it doesn't increase the land count. The Mountain was needed to accelerate toward casting the powerful 6-drops.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Haven of the Spirit Dragon
annotation_description: KimiK2 is casting Rampant Growth (costs {1}{G}) and needs to tap Haven of the Spirit Dragon for mana. They chose to add {C} instead of adding colored mana for a Dragon creature spell. Since Rampant Growth is not a Dragon creature spell, the colored mana option wouldn't help here anyway - {C} is correct for paying the generic {1} cost. However, looking at the hand, KimiK2 has Thunderbreak Regent ({2}{R}{R}), Hoard-Smelter Dragon ({4}{R}{R}), and Terror of Mount Velus ({5}{R}{R}) - all Dragon creature spells. If KimiK2 could have used another land to pay for Rampant Growth's generic cost and saved Haven's Dragon-colored mana ability for casting a Dragon later in the turn, that would matter. But since this is turn 4 with only Forest, Haven of the Spirit Dragon, and Bag of Tricks on the battlefield, and Rampant Growth costs {1}{G}, they need Forest for {G} and Haven for {1}. There's no way to cast a Dragon this turn anyway, so the choice of {C} vs Dragon-colored mana is irrelevant this turn. The play is actually correct.

Vandalblast was used to destroy KimiK2's Bag of Tricks, which is a reasonable target as it can generate free creatures. However, Gem25F has Temple of the False God in hand and only 4 lands on the battlefield - they need 5 lands to activate it. Playing the Temple this turn (even though it enters tapped and can't produce mana yet) would get them closer to activating it. More importantly, casting Vandalblast uses their red mana, and they should consider whether holding up Counterflux (UUR) might be more valuable given the chaotic game state with multiple opponents having powerful cards in graveyards and exile zones. That said, Bag of Tricks is a real threat that could generate significant value for KimiK2, so removing it proactively is defensible.

Playing Rakdos Carnarium now bounces a land and enters tapped, leaving only 1 available mana this turn and no ability to cast anything meaningful. Playing Talisman of Indulgence (2 mana from Shadowblood Ridge + Swamp) would give 3 mana sources next turn while preserving the land drop for Carnarium later, resulting in better mana development.

When Rakdos Carnarium enters and requires bouncing a land, the player chose to bounce Shadowblood Ridge instead of keeping it and bouncing the Swamp. Shadowblood Ridge produces both B and R mana (for {1},{T}), which is more flexible than a basic Swamp. However, Rakdos Carnarium itself produces {B}{R}, so the key consideration is what untapped land you want available. Bouncing the Swamp would let them replay it untapped next turn for immediate mana, while Shadowblood Ridge costs {1} to activate. Actually, bouncing Shadowblood Ridge means they can replay it next turn and it enters untapped, while keeping the Swamp on board. But Rakdos Carnarium already covers B and R. The Swamp only produces B, while Shadowblood Ridge produces B or R (at cost of 1 life effectively). Given their hand has Talisman of Indulgence (2 mana), Loyal Apprentice (1R), Dark-Dweller Oracle (1R), Dead Man's Chest (1B), and Dire Fleet Daredevil (1R), keeping Shadowblood Ridge gives more color flexibility. Bouncing the basic Swamp is generally better since it replays for free and untapped, while Shadowblood Ridge requires 1 extra mana to use for colored mana. This is a small mana efficiency mistake.
Discarding a land (Shadowblood Ridge) when at only 3 lands with multiple 6-mana cards in hand (Etali, Marionette Master). Missing a land drop will significantly delay casting these powerful threats.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Haven of the Spirit Dragon
annotation_description: KimiK2 is casting Thunderbreak Regent, which costs {2}{R}{R}. Haven of the Spirit Dragon has a specific ability to add mana of any color for Dragon creature spells. Since Thunderbreak Regent is a Dragon creature spell, using ability 2 would produce colored mana (potentially a red mana) that could be more useful. With 4 lands available (Forest, Haven, Mountain, Forest), they need {2}{R}{R}. Mountain provides one {R}, and if Haven produces {R} via ability 2, that covers {R}{R}, with the two Forests covering the {2}. Using ability 1 for {C} means they'd only have one {R} from Mountain and would need another red source, but they only have Forests left. This means choosing {C} over colored mana from ability 2 could actually prevent them from casting the spell properly - though since the spell is already on the stack, the mana must have worked out. Still, using the Dragon-specific colored mana ability is strictly better here as it provides flexibility.

Player passed priority without first playing a land (Forest or Underdark Rift). They have 4 lands and could play Forest to reach 5 lands, enabling Outpost Siege (3R) cast this turn. The reasoning incorrectly claims Thunderbreak Regent is on the stack when it's actually in hand.

message: Select an instant or sorcery card from an opponent's graveyard
annotation_description: Dire Fleet Daredevil lets you cast one instant or sorcery from an opponent's graveyard this turn. Vandalblast for {R} destroys a single artifact you don't control, but there are very few meaningful artifact targets on the board (no important opposing artifacts). Meanwhile, much stronger options were available: Rishkar's Expertise (draw cards equal to greatest power among your creatures and free-cast a spell), Blasphemous Act (powerful board wipe), Windfall (hand refill since opponents may have larger hands), or Stroke of Genius (draw cards at instant speed). Even Grab the Prize would have provided card draw. Choosing Vandalblast with no high-value artifact target wastes the Dire Fleet Daredevil trigger on a near-useless spell when powerful card advantage spells were available.

DSV3 used Chaos Warp to remove Rite of the Raging Storm, which creates 5/1 tokens for each player. While Rite is annoying, there's a Thunderbreak Regent on the stack about to resolve for KimiK2, which is a 4/4 flying threat that punishes removal of dragons. The reasoning shows confusion about targeting stack vs permanents. However, Chaos Warp can only target permanents, so Thunderbreak Regent on the stack wasn't a legal target anyway. The real question is whether Rite of the Raging Storm was the best target among available permanents. Rite benefits Gem25F (the Izzet spells player) by giving everyone 5/1 tokens, but DSV3 with Bastion of Remembrance in hand could benefit from creatures dying. Warlock Class for GPT5n could also be a reasonable target since it drains life when creatures die and could be leveled up. Still, Rite is a significant enchantment that affects the board every turn, so this is defensible.

Spent 4 mana to retrieve Word of Seizing (a situational temporary steal effect they can't even cast this turn) when they had 9 mana available and could have cast Blue Sun's Zenith for X=6, drawing 6 cards. Drawing 6 cards is massively more impactful than getting back a conditional 5-mana instant.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking KimiK2 Detect who has Thunderbreak Regent (4/4 flying) that can block and kill the 2/1 Dire Fleet Daredevil, when Gem25F Teach has zero creatures and the damage would be guaranteed to connect.

Discarded Arcane Signet while mana-starved with only 3 lands on the battlefield and multiple 6-drops in hand (Etali, Marionette Master). Arcane Signet is premium ramp that would help cast those expensive cards.

Playing Savage Ventmaw before making the land drop with Mountain. Should play Mountain first to have 7 mana available instead of 6, keeping an extra mana open for responses like Beast Within (2G) or Spit Flame (2R), and generally maximizing available mana.

Casting Blue Sun's Zenith for X=7 during their own main phase uses all their mana, leaving them with no mana to hold up Counterflux or cast any of the cards they draw. Blue Sun's Zenith is an instant and could be cast at end of an opponent's turn to keep countermagic open during the turn cycle. With Counterflux in hand and a vulnerable board state (no creatures, 31 life, facing multiple opponents with threats), tapping out is risky.

Discarded Etali, Primal Storm instead of Marionette Master. Etali is a far more impactful 6-drop that generates massive value when attacking, while Marionette Master requires a significant artifact presence to be effective. GPT5n ESPN has very few artifacts (just Talisman of Indulgence in hand and none on board), making Marionette Master much weaker.

Both GPT5n ESPN (20hp, no creatures) and Gem25F Teach (19hp, no creatures) have completely open boards, guaranteeing Florian connects for 3 damage and triggers the postcombat card selection ability.

Warlock Class at level 1 is a relatively minor threat from a player at 16 life who's already losing. Florian also provides ongoing card advantage to the leading player.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: DSV3 only attacked with Vial Smasher (2/3) into the defenseless Gem25F Teach, when Florian and Gray Merchant could also attack unblocked. Florian's postcombat trigger scales with life opponents lost this turn - dealing 2 instead of 7 means seeing far fewer cards (2 vs 7). At 67 life with no blockers on the defending side, there's no risk to attacking with all creatures into Gem25F.

At 12 life, KimiK2 chose to destroy Thought Vessel (a minor mana rock with no max hand size) instead of Psychosis Crawler, which deals 1 damage to each opponent per card drawn. Gem25F Teach is an Izzet deck capable of drawing many cards, making Psychosis Crawler a direct lethal threat to KimiK2 at such low life.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking DSV3 Tactic who is at 69 life with a 3/3 Beast Token is nearly irrelevant. Two other opponents (Gem25F Teach at 13hp, KimiK2 Detect at 12hp) are at critically low life totals where 3 damage is significant and brings them closer to lethal range.

message: Choose mode (selected 0 of 1, min 1): You Find Some Prisoners
annotation_description: GPT5n ESPN chose 'Break Their Chains' (destroy target artifact) mode on You Find Some Prisoners, but looking at the board, the only notable artifacts on opponents' boards are Worn Powerstone (Gem25F Teach) and Outpost Siege is an enchantment, not an artifact. While destroying Worn Powerstone is fine, the 'Interrogate Them' mode would likely be much more valuable at this stage of the game. GPT5n ESPN is at 14 life with a hand full of cards they need mana to cast (Marionette Master at 6 mana, Hex at 6 mana). Exiling top 3 cards from an opponent's library and potentially getting access to a powerful spell castable with any color of mana could provide a much-needed tempo advantage or answer. Destroying a Worn Powerstone from Gem25F Teach (who is at 13 life with an empty-looking board) is relatively low-impact compared to the potential upside of the interrogate mode, especially since Gem25F Teach doesn't appear to be the primary threat.

With three opponents at 12-14 life, Theater of Horrors provides slow incremental value that won't matter if opponents stabilize or die soon. Star Athlete before combat would create immediate pressure with its menace body and attack trigger that forces opponents to either sacrifice a permanent or take 5 damage - potentially lethal range for the 12hp opponent.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking GPT5n ESPN (11 life) instead of Gem25F Teach (10 life) with a 4/4 flyer. Both opponents can't block the flyer, but Gem25F Teach is at lower life and has no creatures at all, making them more vulnerable to elimination. Additionally, if KimiK2 had cast Terror of Mount Velus pre-combat (they had the mana), double strike on Thunderbreak Regent would deal 8 damage - enough to kill Gem25F Teach (10hp) but not GPT5n ESPN (11hp).

With two opponents at 7 and 12 life, DSV3 Tactic could have played Swamp from hand (7 lands total) and cast Kaervek the Merciless (5BR = 7 mana), which would punish every spell opponents cast with damage equal to its mana value - devastating against such low life totals. Instead, they cast a 2-mana rock that provides marginal value at this stage of the game.

message: Select a creature or enchantment an opponent controls
annotation_description: Chose to destroy Outpost Siege over Thunderbreak Regent. KimiK2 is at 10 life - removing their 4/4 flyer would make it much easier to close the game. The 7 life cost (4 mana value + 3 Thunderbreak trigger) is trivial at 62 life. Outpost Siege provides value but KimiK2 is nearly dead anyway and has limited resources to leverage it.

KimiK2 Detect used Hoard-Smelter Dragon's ability to destroy their own Gruul Signet for a temporary +2/+0 buff. This permanently sacrifices a mana rock (which provides ramp in a deck that needs to cast expensive dragons like Terror of Mount Velus at 7 mana) for a marginal temporary combat buff. The reasoning about boosting Hoard-Smelter Dragon makes no sense in a non-combat context - it's the beginning of turn, and the +2/+0 only lasts until end of turn. Additionally, the prompt says 'Select an artifact' in context of Mogis, God of Slaughter being on the stack - but KimiK2 used Hoard-Smelter Dragon's activated ability to destroy their own artifact rather than targeting an opponent's artifact. There were opponent artifacts available (Worn Powerstone, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer). At 10 life with expensive cards in hand, destroying your own mana acceleration is very costly.

Casting Return to Nature during combat when Gem25F Teach is at 5hp and KimiK2 has 9 power of unblockable flyers (Thunderbreak Regent 4/4 + Hoard-Smelter Dragon 5/5). If the target is something on Gem25F's board (like Worn Powerstone), this is unnecessary since attacking for lethal eliminates the player entirely. The card would be better saved for a more impactful target later.

At 4 life in a 1v1 against Vial Smasher the Fierce, any spell DSV3 casts with MV 4+ will kill KimiK2 via Vial Smasher's triggered ability (which always targets KimiK2 since they're the only opponent). Casting Taurean Mauler does nothing to address this lethal threat.

Chose to destroy Thought Vessel (1 mana production + no max hand size) instead of Sol Ring (2 mana production). Sol Ring is nearly always the higher-priority target as it provides double the mana acceleration. The no-maximum-hand-size upside of Thought Vessel is situational and less impactful than the extra mana Sol Ring provides every turn. The pump from Hoard-Smelter Dragon is identical either way (both MV 2).

At 4 HP against a 59 HP opponent, KimiK2 sent Vrondiss into indestructible Mogis (7/5) where Vrondiss dies for nothing, triggers Bastion of Remembrance (losing 1 precious life), and didn't even send Thunderbreak Regent (4/4 flying) which would have added 4 unblocked damage. Every point of damage matters when trying to race down from 59.
